# dsh-eli5 — plain words
**English · 中文**
Select a word, a sentence, a piece of code or an error message in the DSH Web UI, click the `✦`, and
pick one of four actions from the wheel. A side panel answers in the plainest words it can, and you
can keep asking follow-ups. When the answer depends on the repository, it reads the conversation's
workspace **read-only** and shows exactly what it opened under "looked at".
The name is Explain Like I'm 5, but the point is not baby talk: the first line has to be plain speec
h — "this thing is …" — with no unexplained jargon, and any term that must appear gets translated on
the spot. No guessing, no jargon padding, no restating your question.
The other reason it exists: **it never touches the main conversation**. Answers come from a separate
auxiliary model call; nothing is appended to the Session, so the turn count, token usage and compac
tion threshold of the conversation you are reading do not move.
## Two paths
| | Main conversation | dsh-eli5 |
| Entry | you send from the composer | select text → click `✦` → pick an action (or `Ctrl/⌘+Shift+E`

to explain directly) |
| Goes to | Agent loop → Session log → next request's context | `POST /eli5/

ask` → an independent `ctx.llm.prepareCall` query (plus a few read-only tool rounds when needed) |
|
Messages | system prompt + full history + tool definitions | fixed system prompt + one user message

(+ the panel's own tool rounds) |
| Sees | the whole session | **the conversation on your screen**
(an excerpt read from the DOM) + the selection + the panel's own turns + read-only files under the s

ession cwd |
| Result lands in | Session events (compacted, counted) | browser memory only (plus an

80-entry in-process cache on the host) |
| Effect on context | grows every turn | **none** |
Requests never write to Session storage. The only external things they read are the excerpt of the c
onversation visible on your screen and the files of that session's workspace. Both are sent once and
discarded; neither is written back.
The cost is worth stating too: explanations are billed against the configured model; panel history i
s not persisted and dies with the page or the host process (an identical selection with no tool use
hits the in-process cache instead of paying twice).
## The wheel
Selecting text floats a small `✦` dot next to the selection. Click it and the menu grows out of the
dot: four sectors, each with a one-line hint.
| Action | What it does | Reads the workspace |

| Explain | says what the thing is, in plain words (the original behaviour) | yes |
| Translate | re

nders it in Chinese, keeping code, paths and identifiers verbatim | no |
| Find mistakes | states "w

rong / not wrong / not enough evidence" first, then points at each problem | yes |
| Summarize | one
-line conclusion plus at most three points you can carry away | no |
Keyboard: `1`–`4` pick directly, `Esc` or the hub cancels, clicking elsewhere dismisses. The panel t
itle becomes the action name, and follow-ups stay inside that action — asking "why is it translated
this way" in Translate asks about the translation.
The last column is a whitelist: reading a repository adds nothing to a translation or a summary, so
those two never mount tools and never spend a few extra seconds looking for "more accuracy".
## Reading the workspace (read-only)
The same word means different things in different conversations, and the same symbol behaves differe
ntly in different repositories. The model therefore gets three **read-only** tools:
| Tool | Purpose |
| `read_file(path, startLine?, endLine?)` | reads a text file with line numbers, at most 400 lines p

er call |
| `grep(pattern, glob?, maxResults?)` | regex search, returns `path:line:content`, 40 resu

lts by default |
| `glob(pattern)` | lists files by glob (at most 100) |
The boundary is code, not prompt text:
- **Root = the session's cwd** (read once from the Session header). Anything outside it is refused:

`../`, absolute paths, symlinks pointing out.
- `.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa*`, `.npmrc` and f

riends are refused; `.git`, `node_modules`, `.venv`, `dist` are not entered.
- **Budgets are fixed,
not left to the model**: at most 3 tool rounds, 6 calls, 200 KB read and 60 s in total. When a budge
t runs out, the model receives "budget exhausted, answer from what you have" as a tool result and mu

st wrap up.
- A single tool result over 12 KB is truncated; `grep` also caps its scan at 800 files /

8 MB so it cannot spin inside a large repository.
- Resolution failures, missing files and exhauste
d budgets never throw at the browser: they become a line of text the model can read, so **it cannot
pretend it read something**.
The panel shows "looked at · N succeeded" with one line per call (`read internal/worker/retry.go`, `
search /RetryPolicy/`), failures in red; the block is hidden when nothing was read.
When reading is worth it is constrained by the prompt: answer first, read only when the selection al
one cannot settle the question (behaviour of code, a definition in this repository, "where is this i
mplemented"), one or two files at most, and cite evidence as `path:line`.
